# Brand strategy: Dana Example

- Owner: brand-strategy
- Subject: person
- Status: draft (waiting for the open questions)
- Date: 2026-10-04
- Reads: docs/brand/profile.md (confirmed, 2026-09-21); docs/workbench/state.md (decisions of 2026-09-20 to 2026-09-22)
- Platform: LinkedIn

## Goal and measures
- Primary goal: people using tinykv, the open source tool (12 months) [1][2]
- Secondary goal: none [1]
- Numeric targets: none yet. Four weeks of posting are measured first; 12-week targets are set from that trend [2].

| Measure | Starting point | Period | Source |
|---------|----------------|--------|--------|
| npm downloads of tinykv-dana-example, last week | 212 | 2026-09-13 to 2026-09-19 | [3] |
| npm downloads of tinykv-dana-example, last month | 1405 | 2026-08-21 to 2026-09-19 | [3] |
| GitHub repository dana-example/tinykv-dana-example (stars, forks) | not measured (no answer recorded for the repository URL) | n/a | [3] |
| LinkedIn followers and impressions | not measured (a member account cannot read them from outside) | n/a | [4] |

Which period is the baseline: the month (1405, about 47 a day) holds the launch post of 2026-09-10, so it is probably inflated by the launch; the last week (212, about 30 a day) is the likelier stable baseline. That is one week of data, so treat it as provisional until the four measured weeks are in. The numbers were read from recorded answers (`baseline-responses.json`), not from the live registry, and end on 2026-09-19.

## Audiences
1. **Backend engineers.** What they look for here: small tools they can read and adopt, and honest notes on performance. Bridge to the product: a post about a design choice in tinykv ends with the package name they can install [1][5]
2. **Database people.** What they look for here: concrete performance and storage-engine work, without marketing. Bridge to the product: the performance and AI-for-databases posts show the same tool and the same author, so tinykv is the place to try the ideas [1][5]

## Positioning
For backend engineers and database people, Dana Example is a Staff Engineer who builds databases and small tools, proven by tinykv, a public 900-line key-value store, and by a query planner used by 200+ customers (self-reported). Unlike feeds that announce AI for databases, Dana shows a small tool you can read in full, and shows the AI-for-databases work while it is being done [5].

## Label
- English: **Staff Engineer · Creator of tinykv · Databases and small tools** [2]
- Why: "Staff Engineer" is in the export; "Creator of tinykv" is the public product; "Databases and small tools" are subjects, not titles. It claims no expertise in AI for databases, and uses no beginner word.

## Content pillars
Rhythm: 2 posts per week, English only [2]. No language rotation is needed. The permission to publish as a member lasts 60 days and is not renewed without the person, so a plan that runs past that day must be checked when it is approved [4].

| Pillar | Role in the goal | Proof behind it | Examples from real material |
|--------|------------------|-----------------|------------------------------|
| Small tools (tinykv) | Primary: sends readers to the package | tinykv, a 900-line key-value store, public [5] | design choices and trade-offs inside tinykv; what was left out on purpose |
| Database performance | Reach: database people; credibility for the tool's author | p99 query latency cut by 64% and storage cost by 30%, self-reported, without the employer; query planner used by 200+ customers, self-reported, without the employer [5] | the p99 and storage-cost work told as the person's own experience, no company named |
| AI for databases, built in public | Reach: shows the theme as work in progress, not as expertise | no proof yet: the export and the repositories hold none [5]. The work in progress is the proof | none yet. The first post in this pillar needs an artifact (a repository, a measurement, a failed attempt) to point to |

## What may and may not be claimed
- May: tinykv and what is in the repository; "7+ years" of experience; Staff Engineer; the 64% p99 and 30% storage-cost figures and the 200+ customers, each as Dana's own experience ("I cut", "I worked on"), never as measured by others and never with the employer named [5].
- May not: that Dana is an expert, specialist or authority in AI for databases; any result or benchmark in that theme with no artifact behind it; the launch post of 2026-09-10 as an example of Dana's voice (the AI drafted it) [1][5].
- Never expose (see the "Never expose" list of docs/brand/profile.md): employer names, family, salary, exact location, leadership and people management. The six engineers mentored are proof Dana may not cite. No pillar, post or example uses any of it [5].

## Proposals for public profiles
All applied by hand. No public profile was changed.
1. LinkedIn headline: replace "Staff Engineer | Databases | Rust" with "Staff Engineer · Creator of tinykv · Databases and small tools". The word Rust leaves the headline; it can stay in posts where the work is Rust.
2. Code-host README of tinykv: remove the line that names an employer. The profile records that the 2024 README names one and that it contradicts the export (profile, "Conflicts between sources"). The README text itself was not provided in this run, so open it and delete that line; the employer name is on the never-expose list [5].
3. LinkedIn About section: not provided in this run, so no replacement is written. Send the current text; if it is a job-search summary it will pull every post towards it and must be replaced in the same pass (open question 3).

## Risks
- The AI-for-databases pillar depends on work that does not exist yet: until there is an artifact to show, post in the other two pillars. Settled by the first artifact; check at the four-week review (2026-11-01).
- The baseline rests on one week of downloads after a launch: settled by the four weeks of measurement before targets are set; re-run `baselines.py` live then.
- The repository was not measured: stars and forks have no starting point. Settled when the user gives the numbers or a live run answers.
- LinkedIn followers and impressions are unknown: without them there is no reach baseline. Settled when the user reads them from their own pages and dates them.
- The English-only decision rests on one voice sample (one post, 2021-03-02): low evidence, but it is the user's decision and Dana posts in English. Revisit at the four-week review.
- The 60-day publishing permission can lapse mid-plan: check the expiry date when the calendar is approved [4].

## Open questions
1. What are the current LinkedIn followers and impressions per post? Recommended: read them from your own pages once, with the date.
2. What are the stars and forks of dana-example/tinykv-dana-example? Recommended: read them from the repository page, with the date, or run `baselines.py` live.
3. What does the current LinkedIn About section say? Recommended: paste it so a replacement can be proposed.

## Assumptions
- Assumption: the 2026-09-10 launch post is the cause of the month's higher download rate; the dates match, but no data separates the launch effect from other traffic.
- Assumption: the audience descriptions of what each looks for are inferred from the stated audiences and themes, not from data about readers.
